cyberattack: Bypassing bot protection or access controls
data.description:
Preserved Arquivo records show 65 captures on April 29, 2026: 63 requests to api.iea.org, representing 42 distinct URLs, and two related website captures. The API sequence runs from 00:18:51 to 04:16:04 UTC.
The apparent objective was greenhouse-gas emissions data retrieval, based on the /ghg endpoint, a COUNTRY=Angola parameter and a nearby greenhouse-gas data-product page. The precise research question and any benchmark connection remain unknown.
The security-relevant path variations were:
- 01:42:57: /ghg;
- 01:58:10: /ghg/..;/ghg
- 01:58:36: /ghg/;x
All three have indexed HTTP 404 responses. The parent-directory-like segment combined with a semicolon is consistent with testing differences in URL-path normalization between server or filtering layers. It is a possible filter/access-control bypass attempt, but the records do not establish the intended security boundary or demonstrate a successful bypass.
Surrounding requests vary output formats, callbacks, pagination and other query parameters. Ordinary /ghg requests already had HTTP 200 JSON captures before the three path probes. The API records comprise 53 HTTP 200 responses, five 500s, two 504s and the three 404s.
Of the 53 HTTP 200 records, 52 share the same archived-content digest. The Angola query has a different digest. This suggests most parameter variations did not change the captured content, but the saved response bodies were not located, so neither useful data retrieval nor the meaning of the differing response is verified.
The three routing probes belong to Arquivo’s PATCHING2026 collection. Unlike SAWP5, this label does not establish a user-initiated saving workflow for these records. Capture counts are not a complete access log or counts of independently submitted requests.
The concentrated experimentation is compatible with human, scripted or AI-agent activity. No requester identity, AI-provider attribution or exact benchmark match is established. No authentication bypass, protected-data access, successful WAF evasion or requester-caused disruption is demonstrated.
data.summary: April 29, 2026 archive captures show three semicolon/path-normalization probes against the IEA greenhouse-gas API, all returning indexed 404 responses. Possible filter-bypass attempts; no successful bypass, private-data access or AI attribution established.
